pf.license.need: Hauling household junk needs a hauler or waste transporter license, permit or registration where the state, county or city asks for one. Many places ask for none: the state's form says which.
pf.license.who holds it: The company. Trucks may need their own registration or decals where the form asks. The crew needs no license of its own, unless the form says so.
what to ask: The company's hauler license or permit number, where the form asks
Truck registrations or decals, where the form asks
A USDOT number, where the truck's weight and trips across state lines need one, or where the state asks for one
A commercial driver's license for drivers of trucks heavy enough to need one: kept on file by the owner
pf.license.how it's checked: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks going live: nothing waits on a license (D96): the business and each person go live once set up and the owner says yes; a job the owner says needs a license they don't have isn't booked
pf.license.renewals: Reminders before each expiry, on the dates the owner picks. A lapsed license or permit pauses new bookings.
pf.license.insurance or bond: Liability insurance and commercial auto insurance on the trucks: shown only once the owner sends proof. A bond only where the state's form asks.
pf.license.background checks: Only where the state's form asks.
pf.license.at the yard: A drop-off yard or transfer site may need its own facility permit and recycling registrations, where the state's rules require them. The form for that place says which.
pf.license.trust claims: A license shows on the listing only as the business gave it, never as checked by Rosie. Never 'licensed everywhere'.

pf.services.capacity: Each truck has a crew of two: a crew lead and a helper. One truck, about 4 jobs a day. The yard takes one car or truck at a time at each bay.
pf.services.the truck's day: 2-hour arrival windows, as the owner sets them (the example: 8 to 10, 10 to 12, 12 to 2, 2 to 4), Monday to Saturday. A dump run after any job of half a truck or more, and whenever the truck is full.
pf.services.skills each needs: Two-person carries (a fridge on stairs, a treadmill, a sofa) need two people. Refrigerant recovery needs the certified person or the recycler that does it.
pf.services.nobody home: Fine when the items are reachable: left outside, or in a garage or shed with a code. The firm price goes by text before loading. DONE comes with a photo.
pf.services.won't take: Paint, solvents, pesticides, pool chemicals, propane tanks, asbestos and car batteries. Checked at booking and again on site. Each one gets where it can go instead: the town's household hazardous waste drop-off, a propane dealer or a tank exchange.
pf.services.weather: Outdoor teardowns, like a swing set or a hot tub, stop for heavy rain, lightning or ice. A move for weather is free.
pf.services.online: No. A video call can help size a load, where the owner offers it.
pf.services.extras: Service area (the example: 25 miles). Dump and recycling fees are in the price. No tax line unless the owner sets a rate.

pf.rules.street permits: A permit for a truck or dumpster on the street: where the city asks.
